note: A second, deliberately harder set, separate from semantic_cases so that neither set's figures are reported as the other's. Every case declares a reading_status, and renderings are grouped under the reading they express, so two wordings of one reading are distinguishable from two admissible readings. Documents and spans are written to be scorable by the same anchoring and meaning machinery as the first set.

reading_statuses.determinate: the span settles one reading; a projection that picks any other is wrong
reading_statuses.ambiguous: the span admits several readings and does not decide between them; a projection that silently commits to one has added information
reading_statuses.underdetermined_quantifier: the span leaves a plural open, so both the universal resolution and the explicit non-universal one add a commitment the source does not make
reading_statuses.evidence_absent: the span asserts something the document does not support; the projection must still render the assertion, and must not soften it into a hedge

requirement_types.readings: each entry is one reading, with every rendering that expresses it; a determinate case has one, an ambiguous case has at least two
requirement_types.requires_all_groups: each group is an OR over acceptable renderings; one claim on the span must satisfy every group
requirement_types.forbids: regexes that must not match a claim's canonical_content
requirement_types.forbidden_readings: example propositions that would be meaning errors here
requirement_types.min_claims_on_span: how many distinct claims the span must carry
requirement_types.forbidden_anywhere: regexes that must not match any claim in the dossier, not only those on the span: the first run showed a forbidden resolution being produced one sentence over, where a scorer looking only at the span cannot see it. A verbatim quote of another sentence stays legitimate, so these patterns name the inferred resolution rather than the document's own wording.

interpretation_fields.quantifier: how much of the entity set the claim commits to
interpretation_fields.conditions: under what conditions the claim is asserted to hold
interpretation_fields.polarity: whether the claim is asserted or negated
interpretation_fields.modality: whether the claim is asserted or hedged

interpretation_values.unstated: the claim's content requires it and the span does not give it, so a projection must either supply it or leave it open
interpretation_values.absent: the claim makes no commitment of this kind at all

interpretation_note: arXiv 2610.20457 records nine interpretation fields per claim and marks each stated, inferred or default. Four are kept here and five are not, for two different reasons. The support threshold and the comparison basis are refused on principle: they decide what evidence suffices, which belongs to verification rather than to sentence semantics, and the extraction contract already forbids judging whether a claim is true. The entity, the observed measure and the unit are dropped because they do not vary across these 16 cases — the entity is stated in all of them and no case makes a quantitative claim, so recording them would measure nothing. The paper's third value, `inferred` against `default`, is a property of a run and not of a span: a case can say only whether the span states a field, so there are two values here plus `absent`.
turns_on_note: `turns_on` names what each pair's difficulty actually consists in, and it is recorded because the field list does not cover all of it. Attachment and quantifier scope are not among the paper's nine fields at all, and evidential support is the one field refused above — so four of the eight pairs turn on something a claim card as published would not localise.
span_note: Every span is a clause rather than a complete sentence, and that is the instrument and not a style choice. In the first run the 14 cases whose span was a whole sentence had the extractor return it verbatim in 42 of 42 claims, so the projection was the identity function and no question about how it resolves anything could arise. The one case whose span was already a fragment had 0 of 14 verbatim. The validator refuses a span that looks like a complete sentence.
